paragraphs: This paper develops a practical approximation to AIXI, a Bayesian notion of an optimal reinforcement learning agent. Its focus is on environments with complex structure and dependence on past events. In these settings, choosing a useful description of the current situation is an important part of making effective decisions.

The approach uses higher-order logic to define and enumerate features of an environment. These features can describe structured situations and information from history. The method then adapts a criterion from state abstraction theory to select a subset of features, producing a more manageable state representation for learning.

A generalized Context Tree Weighting method performs exact Bayesian model learning over the resulting abstract state sequences. The architecture can work with different planning algorithms, separating the representation and learning machinery from the choice of planner. Experiments on epidemic control in large contact networks support the agent's performance. The contribution is a way to expand the environments covered by practical AIXI approximations, rather than a claim to implement unrestricted AIXI.
neurips-2022-a-direct-approximation-of-a.tldr: Logical state abstractions extend a practical AIXI approximation to structured environments whose behavior depends on history.

paragraphs: The Cross-Entropy Method plans by sampling candidate solutions and updating a sampling distribution using the best candidates. This paper argues that a centralized update can make the search vulnerable to local optima: promising samples can pull the search toward a region that is good without being globally best. That can waste samples.

DecentCEM replaces this centralized search with an ensemble of independent CEM instances. Each instance improves its own sampling distribution, so the search does not depend on one shared update. The authors provide theoretical and empirical analysis of this design. In their experiments, it finds the global optimum more consistently than centralized alternatives using either one Gaussian distribution or a mixture.

The authors also substitute DecentCEM for the planning component in model-based reinforcement learning and test it in continuous control environments. Comparisons with PETS and POPLIN show improved sample efficiency, at an additional computational cost described as reasonable. The findings suggest that changing how candidate searches are coordinated can improve learning efficiency without replacing the surrounding reinforcement learning approach.
neurips-2022-a-simple-decentralized-cros.tldr: Independent CEM searches improve global-optimum discovery and reinforcement learning sample efficiency in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: AMOS addresses a problem in evaluating medical image segmentation: available datasets often cover too few scans or organs to assess models across varied clinical situations. Segmentation assigns anatomical labels throughout an image. For three-dimensional abdominal scans, collecting data and labeling individual volume elements is expensive, which makes broad benchmarks difficult to build.

The dataset contains 500 CT scans and 100 MRI scans, each annotated at the voxel level for 15 abdominal organs. It brings together scans from multiple centers and scanner vendors, as well as different imaging modalities, phases, and disease settings. This variety creates a test environment with multiple sources of clinical and imaging variation.

The authors benchmark several leading medical segmentation models on AMOS and release the data, benchmark servers, and baseline methods. The contribution is a shared resource for examining how existing approaches perform across diverse targets and scenarios. It supports more comprehensive comparisons and research on robust segmentation; the abstract does not present a new segmentation algorithm as the central result.
neurips-2022-amos-a-large-scale-abdomina.tldr: AMOS provides 600 annotated CT and MRI scans for evaluating abdominal organ segmentation across diverse clinical settings.

paragraphs: Model fingerprinting asks whether a suspicious model was derived from an owner's model. This paper targets weaknesses in fingerprints based on transferable adversarial examples, which can be sensitive to adversarial defenses or transfer learning. Its alternative examines relationships between model outputs across multiple input samples.

The proposed Sample Correlation method, SAC, has two versions. SAC-w uses ordinary samples that a model classifies incorrectly and calculates the average correlation among their outputs. SAC-m uses CutMix-augmented samples to reduce preparation time. That version avoids both training surrogate models and generating adversarial examples, making the fingerprinting procedure simpler to prepare.

Across the evaluated datasets and architectures, SAC detects stolen models under several attack settings, including adversarial training and transfer learning. The authors report the best detection performance in terms of AUC among the compared methods. The central finding is that correlations across responses can provide useful evidence of model derivation even in settings that challenge adversarial-example fingerprints. This is evidence for detecting theft in the tested settings, rather than preventing a model from being copied.
neurips-2022-are-you-stealing-my-model-s.tldr: SAC fingerprints models through correlations between sample outputs, detecting stolen models across several tested attack settings.

paragraphs: Personalizing an image classifier often means adapting a pretrained system using only a few labeled examples from a user. Accuracy matters, but so does the computation required for adaptation. This paper studies that trade-off, aiming to improve classification while keeping the cost of learning a new task low.

Its Contextual Squeeze-and-Excitation block, CaSE, uses the new task's examples as context to adjust the network. After meta-training, these blocks can adapt the network body with a single forward pass of the context data. The complete method, UpperCaSE, combines that conditional adaptation with a separate fine-tuning routine for a linear prediction head.

UpperCaSE achieves the strongest reported accuracy relative to meta-learning competitors across the 26 datasets of VTAB+MD and the ORBIT personalization benchmark. It also narrows the accuracy gap with leading fine-tuning methods while requiring orders of magnitude less adaptation computation. The single-pass result applies to adaptation through CaSE blocks; the overall method still includes fine-tuning its head. Together, these findings improve the demonstrated balance between accuracy and adaptation cost.
neurips-2022-contextual-squeeze-and-exci.tldr: UpperCaSE uses context-conditioned network blocks to improve few-shot classification with much lower adaptation cost than leading fine-tuning methods.

paragraphs: Structured pruning compresses a pretrained neural network by removing neurons or channels. Many approaches rely on subsequent fine-tuning, which becomes difficult when little training data is available. This paper develops a pruning method that uses a limited amount of unlabeled data and provides theoretical guarantees under stated assumptions.

For each layer, the method jointly chooses which neurons or channels to remove and new weights for the following layer. Its objective is to keep the next layer's input close to what the original network would have produced. The authors show that this selection can be expressed as a weakly submodular maximization problem, allowing an efficient greedy algorithm with a provable approximation guarantee.

Under reasonable assumptions, their analysis bounds the difference between original and compressed model outputs with an error guarantee that decreases exponentially as the pruned model's size increases. Experiments show better performance than the compared leading methods when data is limited. The contribution connects an explicit preservation objective with efficient selection and theoretical support, making compression more practical when extensive labeled data is unavailable.
neurips-2022-data-efficient-structured-p.tldr: A greedy pruning method uses limited unlabeled data to compress networks while providing conditional guarantees on output preservation.

paragraphs: Generating realistic molecular structures requires accounting for the physical laws that govern molecules. This paper studies how to incorporate physical and statistical prior information into the training of diffusion-based generative models. The aim is to guide generation toward structures with better quality and stability.

The proposed mechanism uses physically informed diffusion bridges. A bridge is a stochastic process constructed to reach a specified observation at a fixed terminal time. The authors develop a method based on a Lyapunov function to construct and determine these bridges, then propose several versions carrying useful prior information. This makes prior knowledge part of the training process itself.

Experiments cover both molecule generation and three-dimensional point cloud generation. The authors report improved molecular quality and stability scores, along with high-quality point clouds whose points are distributed more uniformly. These results support diffusion bridges as a useful way to guide different kinds of three-dimensional generation. The endpoint guarantee concerns the constructed stochastic process; the reported improvements in generated structures are experimental findings.
neurips-2022-diffusion-based-molecule-ge.tldr: Physically and statistically informed diffusion bridges improve reported molecular generation scores and point cloud uniformity.

paragraphs: Residual networks are often connected to continuous-time neural ordinary differential equations. This paper asks when that connection accurately describes the network's hidden states. It derives a tight bound on the distance between a ResNet trajectory and its corresponding Neural ODE. Increasing depth alone does not make this bound vanish when residual functions lack smoothness across layers.

A positive result applies to linear residual functions with sufficiently small initial loss. In that setting, gradient descent preserves the required smoothness, producing convergence toward a limiting Neural ODE at a rate proportional to one divided by depth. The guarantee holds uniformly across network depth and optimization time.

The analysis also supports a memory-free discrete adjoint method that reconstructs activations during a backward pass. It succeeds theoretically at large depth when residual functions are Lipschitz in their inputs. With smoothness across depth, Heun's integration method improves gradient estimation. Experiments confirm successful deep-network training and fewer required layers with Heun's method, including fine-tuning very deep ResNets without activation memory consumption in residual layers.
neurips-2022-do-residual-neural-networks.tldr: ResNets approach Neural ODE behavior under specific smoothness conditions, which also support memory-saving training methods.

paragraphs: This paper studies minimax problems where one variable is minimized while another is maximized. The objective is smooth and strongly concave in the maximizing variable, but it may be nonconvex in the minimizing variable. The target is the primal objective: the value obtained after maximizing over the second variable.

The authors propose Minimax Cubic Newton, or MCN, to find approximate second-order stationary points of that primal objective. These points satisfy conditions involving both gradients and curvature, giving a stronger local criterion than first-order stationarity alone. The analysis provides explicit finite-accuracy bounds on the required first-order and second-order oracle calls, with dependence on accuracy, conditioning, and Hessian smoothness.

For high-dimensional problems, an inexact variant avoids expensive full second-order oracle calls. It approximately solves cubic subproblems using gradient descent and matrix Chebyshev expansion, relying instead on Hessian-vector products. This version reaches the desired approximate stationarity with high probability. The contribution is a non-asymptotic convergence analysis beyond convex-concave minimax problems, while retaining the stated strong concavity assumption on the maximizing variable.
neurips-2022-finding-second-order-statio.tldr: Minimax Cubic Newton provides finite-accuracy guarantees for second-order stationarity in smooth nonconvex, strongly concave minimax problems.

paragraphs: This paper approaches classification through concept cognition: the process of recognizing and organizing concepts. The authors argue that, despite the variety of existing classifiers, few fully account for this perspective. They propose the fuzzy learning machine, or FLM, as a classifier designed around that cognitive motivation.

FLM draws inspiration from cognitive science and places its mathematical foundations in set theory and fuzzy set theory. The paper presents these as complementary aspects of the design. The cognitive perspective motivates how the classifier works, while the mathematical framework gives the method a formal basis. The authors describe the resulting working mechanism as strongly interpretable.

Experiments across many datasets show that even a simple implementation can achieve strong classification performance. This supports the paper's central proposition that a classifier organized around concept cognition can also be practically effective. Its contribution combines a particular way of thinking about classification, an explicit mathematical foundation, and empirical evidence of performance. The reported findings support FLM's effectiveness without establishing that it universally outperforms every other classifier.
neurips-2022-fuzzy-learning-machine-ad56.tldr: FLM uses concept cognition and fuzzy set theory to build an interpretable classifier with strong reported experimental performance.

paragraphs: Multitask learning predicts several targets from the same input. This paper examines a specific source of unreliable relationships: unobserved confounders that cause the targets but do not cause the input. Such target-causing confounders can induce spurious input-target dependencies and create problems for methods that assume targets are conditionally independent once the input is known.

Generative multitask learning, GMTL, changes the inference objective rather than the training procedure. It predicts the targets jointly and removes influence from their joint distribution. A single hyperparameter controls the degree of removal, allowing adjustment of the balance between performance on the original distribution and generalization when the target distribution changes.

Because the change occurs at inference time, GMTL can be applied to existing multitask learning methods without additional training. Experiments on Attributes of People and Taskonomy show improved robustness to target shift across four such methods. The result identifies a specific causal mechanism and offers a comparatively small intervention for mitigating it, while preserving flexibility over the trade-off between in-distribution and shifted-data performance.
neurips-2022-generative-multitask-learni.tldr: GMTL changes multitask inference to mitigate target-causing confounding and improve robustness to target shift without retraining.

paragraphs: A model can fit its training observations exactly and still generalize statistically. This paper asks whether the same is true when the goal is causal generalization. It studies minimum-norm interpolators and ridge regression under a simple linear causal model, deriving precise asymptotic expressions for causal risk in a high-dimensional setting.

The analysis introduces a measure of confounding strength that explains different outcomes. When this quantity is positive, interpolators cannot be optimal, and causal learning needs stronger regularization than statistical learning. Positive confounding strength holds under the independent causal mechanisms assumption, so this conclusion applies within an established causal modeling assumption.

Outside that assumption, negative confounding produces a different picture. Positive alignment between statistical and causal signals creates a form of self-induced regularization. Causal learning can then need weaker regularization, exact-fitting models can be optimal, and the optimal regularization can even be negative. The findings show why a regularization choice that works for statistical prediction may be inappropriate for causal learning, with the direction of the difference depending on confounding.
neurips-2022-interpolation-and-regulariz.tldr: In a high-dimensional linear causal model, confounding strength determines whether causal learning needs more or less regularization than statistical prediction.

paragraphs: Group convolutional networks constrain their features to respond consistently to selected transformations. These constraints help when the assumed symmetries match the data, but can hurt when they impose too much structure. For example, images may contain only a limited range of rotations rather than every possible rotation.

Partial G-CNNs learn how much equivariance to retain at each layer during training. They support discrete and continuous transformation groups, including combinations of them. Allowing different layers to learn different amounts matters because useful transformations can change with feature complexity: edge orientations and whole-face poses need not follow the same symmetry assumptions.

The experiments show that the method retains full equivariance when it is useful, as with rotated MNIST, and adjusts it when it becomes harmful, as with distinguishing digits 6 and 9 or classifying natural images. Partial G-CNNs match conventional G-CNNs in the reported settings favoring full equivariance and outperform them otherwise. The contribution makes symmetry constraints adaptable to both the dataset and the level of representation.
neurips-2022-learning-partial-equivarian.tldr: Partial G-CNNs learn layer-specific symmetry constraints, retaining full equivariance when useful and relaxing it when it harms performance.

paragraphs: Behavioral metrics help reinforcement learning systems represent states according to their behavioral relationships. An informative representation can accelerate learning, but turning that idea into a practical method creates two problems. The desired metric may be difficult or intractable to compute, and a learned state embedding must approximate whichever tractable version is used.

This paper analyzes the gaps introduced by those two steps in existing methods. Relaxing a metric can change what it measures, while learning an embedding can introduce additional approximation error. Based on this analysis, the authors propose a new behavioral distance called RAP and develop a practical representation learning algorithm around it, accompanied by theoretical analysis.

The method is evaluated on DeepMind Control Suite with distraction, Robosuite, and the CARLA autonomous driving simulator. The authors report new state-of-the-art results across their experiments. The contribution connects scrutiny of the underlying distance with the design of the learned representation. Its findings support addressing metric relaxation and embedding approximation together when building behavioral representations for deep reinforcement learning.
neurips-2022-learning-representations-vi.tldr: RAP combines a new behavioral distance with practical representation learning, achieving leading reported results across several reinforcement learning environments.

paragraphs: Complex skills often depend on reusing smaller patterns learned earlier. Inspired by cognitive theories of chunking and grouping by proximity, this paper introduces a hierarchical chunking model, HCM. It learns from sequential data whose observations are dependent, beginning with small atomic sequences and building more complex representations from them.

As learning proceeds, HCM combines previously discovered chunks according to sequential dependence. The resulting hierarchy makes the components of a representation explicit and interpretable. The authors establish learning guarantees for an idealized version of the model and demonstrate human-like learning of meaningful chunks. They also describe extensions to visual, temporal, and combined visual-temporal patterns.

Interpretable chunks provide a way to assess whether learned structure transfers or interferes when the environment changes. In an fMRI dataset, HCM discovers chunks of functionally coactive regions and hierarchical modular structures consistent with the neuroscience literature. These findings support chunking as a route to interpretable representation learning, while the formal guarantees specifically concern the idealized model analyzed in the paper.
neurips-2022-learning-structure-from-the.tldr: HCM builds interpretable hierarchies by combining learned sequential chunks into progressively more complex representations.

paragraphs: Handwriting verification aims to distinguish authentic writing from forgeries. This paper argues that small datasets and a narrow selection of handwriting types have limited progress toward practical use. It introduces MSDS, a benchmark that includes both Chinese signatures and handwritten token digit strings.

The dataset has contributions from 402 users. Each user supplies 20 genuine samples and 20 skilled forgeries for each of its two subsets. MSDS-ChS contains Chinese signatures and is described, to the authors' knowledge, as the largest publicly available Chinese signature verification dataset, at least eight times larger than existing online datasets. MSDS-TDS uses handwritten versions of users' actual phone numbers.

The authors evaluate several baseline methods separately on both subsets. Leading verification methods generally perform better on the digit strings than on the Chinese signatures. This suggests that handwritten token digit strings could be a more effective biometric in this setting. Alongside providing a larger shared benchmark, the paper offers evidence that the type of writing being verified deserves attention, rather than treating signatures as the only useful medium.
neurips-2022-msds-a-large-scale-chinese-.tldr: MSDS benchmarks signatures and handwritten phone numbers, with results suggesting digit strings could be a stronger verification biometric.

paragraphs: Object-oriented reinforcement learning represents an environment through its objects and reasons about them to choose actions. This paper focuses on information that individual object representations can overlook: different instances of the same category often have similar functions. The proposed OCARL framework explicitly uses category information in both perception and reasoning.

OCARL has three components. An unsupervised discovery stage identifies objects and their categories. A perception stage encodes category information while remaining robust to incompleteness in that discovery process. Finally, modular reasoning uses multiple independent networks associated with object categories, giving category distinctions a direct role in how the agent reasons.

Experiments in the object-oriented reinforcement learning domain show improvements in both sample efficiency and generalization. These findings support using shared category structure in addition to recognizing individual objects. The design also acknowledges that object discovery may be incomplete, rather than requiring the perception stage to rely on a perfect discovered inventory. The overall contribution is an integrated framework that carries category information from discovery through representation to decision-making.
neurips-2022-object-category-aware-reinf.tldr: OCARL uses object categories throughout perception and reasoning to improve reported reinforcement learning sample efficiency and generalization.

paragraphs: This paper studies online decisions with hard constraints, where violating a constraint now cannot be canceled by being conservative later. It tracks both regret, relative to a comparator's losses, and cumulative violation. The proposed RECOO algorithm handles constraints that stay fixed and constraints chosen adversarially over time.

With fixed constraints, RECOO guarantees regret growing as the square root of the learning horizon and bounded cumulative violation. This improves the previous violation bound while preserving the regret order. With adversarial constraints, it matches the best stated existing orders: square-root regret and violation growing as the horizon to the three-quarter power.

Stronger assumptions yield stronger results. For strongly convex losses, regret becomes logarithmic, with bounded violation for fixed constraints and a square-root-of-horizon-times-logarithm violation bound for adversarial constraints. These guarantees compare against the best fixed decision in hindsight. The paper also analyzes changing comparators, improving fixed-constraint results and providing its claimed first dynamic guarantees for adversarial constraints. Experiments report advantages over several existing algorithms in both constraint settings.
neurips-2022-online-convex-optimization-.tldr: RECOO improves or matches regret and cumulative hard-constraint violation bounds across fixed and adversarial constraint settings.

paragraphs: Imagen combines a large transformer language model with a diffusion image generator to turn text into realistic images. The paper's central finding concerns the text component: language models pretrained only on text, such as T5, can encode descriptions effectively for image synthesis.

In the reported scaling comparisons, increasing the language model's size improves both image fidelity and agreement with the description more than increasing the diffusion model's size. This points to text understanding as an important contributor to generation quality. Imagen achieves a COCO FID score of 7.27 without training on COCO, and human raters judge its image-text alignment to be on par with the dataset's own images.

The authors also introduce DrawBench to examine text-to-image systems more deeply. In side-by-side comparisons with VQ-GAN+CLIP, Latent Diffusion Models, and DALL-E 2, raters prefer Imagen for both image quality and alignment with the text. Together, these results support the architecture and its emphasis on language representation, while the human preferences describe the comparisons performed in the study.
neurips-2022-photorealistic-text-to-imag.tldr: Imagen shows that scaling a text-pretrained language encoder can substantially improve diffusion image quality and text alignment.

paragraphs: ResTv2 is a multi-scale vision Transformer designed as a backbone for visual recognition. The paper simplifies the earlier ResTv1 attention structure by removing its multi-head interaction component. It also adds an upsampling operation intended to reconstruct medium- and high-frequency information lost during downsampling.

The authors investigate how to apply the backbone to downstream tasks and examine the relationship between theoretical computation and actual speed. Combining the revised attention mechanism with window attention can greatly reduce matrix multiplication FLOPs. However, it may also reduce computation density enough to make execution slower. The finding shows why fewer arithmetic operations do not necessarily mean a faster implementation.

Evaluation covers ImageNet image classification, COCO object detection, and ADE20K semantic segmentation. The reported results show substantial gains over recently leading backbones, supporting ResTv2's use across several visual recognition tasks. The contribution combines architectural simplification with an effort to recover information lost through downsampling, while its efficiency analysis emphasizes measuring actual speed alongside theoretical operation counts.
neurips-2022-rest-v2-simpler-faster-and-.tldr: ResTv2 simplifies vision Transformer attention and reconstructs downsampled detail, with strong reported results across three recognition tasks.

paragraphs: Convergence analyses for stochastic gradient descent with momentum often require learning rates whose squared values have a finite sum. This forces the step size to shrink sufficiently quickly, potentially slowing early progress. This paper relaxes that requirement while studying convergence of the last iterate.

The new condition requires summability of step sizes raised to a power of two plus a parameter between zero and one-half, excluding one-half. With a suitable positive parameter, this permits a schedule proportional to one divided by the square root of the iteration count. Under this condition and additional common assumptions, the authors prove that gradient norms approach zero for nonconvex losses. They also show faster early arrival near stationary points.

A separate result studies constant step sizes and establishes convergence without the strong convexity requirement commonly imposed in prior work. Experiments illustrate the theoretical findings. The contribution broadens the step-size choices supported by analysis; the vanishing-gradient result for decaying steps should be distinguished from the separate constant-step convergence claim.
neurips-2022-revisit-last-iterate-conver.tldr: The paper relaxes step-size decay requirements for momentum SGD while proving conditional convergence results and faster early progress.

paragraphs: Generalized additive models are used for interpretable prediction, but the paper argues that their expressiveness and scalability can restrict practical use. Scalable Polynomial Additive Models, or SPAM, aim to retain an inherently interpretable model structure while handling richer relationships among many input features.

SPAM uses tensor rank decompositions of polynomials. This representation allows the model to account for higher-order feature interactions without a combinatorial explosion in parameters. Those interactions matter because a prediction can depend on combinations of features, rather than only on separate feature contributions. The decomposition provides the paper's route to combining interaction modeling with scalability.

On a series of real-world benchmarks containing up to hundreds of thousands of features, SPAM outperforms the compared interpretable approaches and matches the performance of deep neural networks and XGBoost. Human-subject evaluations also support improved practical interpretability. Together, the results show that this polynomial model class can offer competitive predictive performance and understandable structure at large feature counts in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2022-scalable-interpretability-v.tldr: SPAM uses decomposed polynomials to model feature interactions at scale while matching strong predictors on reported benchmarks.

paragraphs: The Yeo-Johnson transformation adjusts individual features to make their distributions more Gaussian-like. Applying it consistently across organizations is challenging when data must remain separated for privacy. This paper develops a federated procedure that fits the transformation as if the organizations' data had been pooled.

The authors first prove that the Yeo-Johnson negative log-likelihood is convex. That result enables an optimization algorithm based on exponential search. Numerical comparisons show greater stability than the existing approach based on Brent minimization. This optimization result forms the computational foundation of the federated method.

SecureFedYJ combines the algorithm with secure multiparty computation. Its privacy guarantee is that the procedure reveals no more information than the final fitted parameters themselves, while producing a pooled-equivalent transformation. Experiments on real data show reliable feature normalization across silos, matching what pooling would achieve. The contribution brings both numerical stability and a specific information-leakage guarantee to a preprocessing step needed before federated model learning, without requiring that the underlying datasets be combined.
neurips-2022-securefedyj-a-safe-feature-.tldr: SecureFedYJ fits pooled-equivalent feature transformations across data silos while revealing no more than the fitted parameters.

paragraphs: This paper studies recovery of a rank-one signal from structured, rotationally invariant noise when an estimator incorrectly assumes Gaussian noise. The question is how much this mismatch costs. The authors rigorously analyze both a Bayes estimator under the incorrect model and an approximate message passing algorithm, or AMP, using the same mistaken assumption.

Their analysis gives sharp asymptotic characterizations of both methods. For the Bayes estimator, it uses spherical integrals and low-rank matrix perturbation theory. For AMP, it constructs an artificial algorithm whose flexible denoisers can correct the mismatch, providing a way to analyze the original method's behavior.

The results distinguish errors in signal magnitude from recovery of its alignment. The mismatched Bayes estimator outperforms AMP in mean-square error, despite AMP's intended role in efficiently computing such estimates. The gap comes from incorrect signal-norm estimation. At sufficiently high signal-to-noise ratios, their overlaps coincide and even match estimators that account for the noise structure. Thus, equal overlap need not imply equal overall estimation error.
neurips-2022-the-price-of-ignorance-how-.tldr: Ignoring structured noise can separate AMP and Bayes estimation errors even when their recovered signal overlaps agree.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning faces a trade-off when real data is scarce and simulators are imperfect. Simulation allows extensive exploration, but simplified dynamics can produce policies that transfer poorly. Offline learning uses historical real-world data, yet effective learning can require broad coverage of states and actions. H2O combines these two sources.

The framework learns from a fixed real-world dataset while also exploring in simulation. Its central mechanism is dynamics-aware policy evaluation: it adaptively penalizes Q-function learning on simulated state-action pairs that have large dynamics gaps. This makes the influence of simulated experience depend on how strongly its dynamics differ from the real environment.

The authors provide theoretical analysis and evaluate H2O in simulation and real-world tasks. They report stronger performance than the compared cross-domain online and offline reinforcement learning algorithms. The findings support using limited real data together with simulator exploration, while adjusting for disagreement between their dynamics. H2O offers a hybrid learning approach in which simulation remains useful even when it is imperfect.
neurips-2022-when-to-trust-your-simulato.tldr: H2O combines fixed real-world data with simulator exploration and penalizes simulated learning where dynamics gaps are large.
